maria (eng-platform): Quick question — we need an SLO-driven routing policy design for customer tiers + region. Goal: keep premium p95 latency < 150ms and availability > 99.5%. When SLOs degrade, route to fallback model variants with graceful backpressure. Thoughts?

devon (eng-runtime): Love the idea. Main API debate: allow per-tenant thresholds, per-route overrides, or only tiered defaults? Per-tenant = flexible but huge config surface.

sasha (product): From console UX POV: we should surface a live "SLO burn" chart, an interactive slider to tune p95 target, and a "simulate fallback" button so customers can preview impact on latency/cost. Also need safe rollbacks. :eyes:

li (eng-ml): Telemetry requirements: p50/p95/p99 decode latencies, queue depth, tokens/sec, model GPU util, variant cold-start latencies, and error/retry rates. Without variant-level metrics we can't reason about fallback effectiveness.

maria (eng-platform): Agree. Also need circuit-breaker hysteresis and cooldown windows to avoid flapping. Proposing policy schema prototype below for discussion.

devon (eng-runtime): Can we see the schema? Prefer JSON-ish so runtime can natively ingest.

maria (eng-platform): ```json
{
  "policy_name": "slo_routing_v1",
  "scopes": ["tenant:premium", "region:us-east-1"],
  "latency_slo_ms": 150,
  "availability_slo_pct": 99.5,
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "p95_latency_ms": 200,
    "error_rate_pct": 1.0,
    "min_requests": 50,
    "cooldown_s": 300
  },
  "fallback": {
    "strategy": "model_variant",
    "variants": ["gpt-medium-quant", "gpt-small-quant"],
    "max_qps": 50
  }
}
```

devon (eng-runtime): Nice. Algorithmically I propose: evaluate moving-window metrics and open CB if (p95 > cb.p95 OR error_pct > cb.error_rate) AND requests >= min_requests. Add a 2x grace window and decay back only when p95 consistently below 90% of target for two windows. Pseudocode:

```
if window.requests >= cb.min_requests and (window.p95 > cb.p95_latency_ms or window.errors_pct > cb.error_rate_pct):
    open_cb()
    route_to(fallback)
elif cb.open and time_since_open > cb.cooldown_s and window.p95 < slo.latency_slo_ms * 0.9:
    close_cb()
```

li (eng-ml): Add per-variant health: if fallback variant has cold-start or high error rate, fallback may be worse. We should require variant-level SLIs and an "opt-out" if variant health < X. Also track cost delta so product knows billing impact.

sasha (product): UX constraints: console should show: current SLO status, active CB state (open/closed), reason (p95/error), time open, affected tenants, and an action to "force open/close" for ops. Heatmap per-region would help.

maria (eng-platform): Good point about quotas. Routing should consult quota checks post-policy decision but pre-enqueue: if a tenant is over quota, route into throttling path rather than fallback to larger model (avoid double-cost).

devon (eng-runtime): Implementation note: make circuit-breaker decisions in the routing layer, not the model host, so we can fail fast and update metrics with single source of truth. We'll need a lightweight shared state (redis/etcd) for CB state.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy push to staging succeeded — https://console.internal/redwood/policies/staging/123 :rocket:

maria (eng-platform): Next steps: devon/li to prototype runtime evaluator + sample policy ingest; sasha to mock console panels; I'll draft an RFC with the schema, CB semantics, and telemetry contract. Can we sync tomorrow 10am?

sasha (product): 10am works. I'll bring a mockup and cost examples. :+1:

li (eng-ml): I'll prepare a list of per-variant SLIs and suggested thresholds.

devon (eng-runtime): I'll prototype evaluator and a simulation harness to replay traces and validate CB behaviour.

maria (eng-platform): Great — adding meeting invite now. Thanks all. :tada:
